Thanks for the detailed history. I appreciate the transparency, but looking at these records, I have serious concerns about the maintenance profile.

Every single entry is a Jiffy Lube oil change. There is zero documentation of any major interval service—most critically, **no CVT fluid exchange**. For a 2016 Altima with 83,223 miles, that is a major red flag. These CVTs are well-documented for premature failure without regular fluid changes, and I’m looking at an immediate **$400–$500 service** to protect the drivetrain, plus the latent risk of a far more expensive repair down the road if the previous interval was missed.

I also don’t see any 60k or 80k service items addressed: no spark plugs, no coolant exchange, no inspection records. The front brakes were done 18,000 miles ago, which is not "recent" at this mileage. The tires are fine, but they have 8,000 miles on them now.

KBB private party on a properly maintained example is $10,990–$12,540. This isn’t a properly maintained example—it’s a quick-lube-only car with a critical drivetrain service gap. Per my earlier note, I don’t split the difference on repair deductions; I subtract the full cost.

My offer is **$10,500**. That reflects the bottom of the KBB range minus the immediate catch-up maintenance I’ll have to perform day one to make this car mechanically sound. I’m ready to close quickly if that works.

Regards,  
Jon Clark
